headline: The US Energy Department has issued an emergency order, running to 16 Oct 2026, that lets the PJM grid operator ask data centers and other large power users to switch to back-up generators if needed to prevent blackouts.
score_reason: Order was issued on 12 Oct 2026, one day before the window, and is conditional and temporary; lowered 1 from 7.
importance_line: Millions of mid-Atlantic households and businesses are the ones the order aims to shield from blackouts, data centers may be told to run on their own generators, and the wording is conditional ('if necessary') so it does not show that any data center has actually been switched over.
summary: The National reports that the US Energy Department issued an emergency order on Monday 12 Oct, in force until 16 Oct, under which PJM, the mid-Atlantic grid operator, can tell data centers and other large power users to switch to back-up generators if needed, as warm weather and planned power-plant maintenance outages strain its grid, and that PJM has also issued a maximum generation alert for 13 and 14 Oct which it says needs no action from customers. Energy Secretary Chris Wright says the order will help keep power affordable and reliable, and the department says the US has 35 gigawatts of unused back-up generation.
notes: Order issued Mon 12 Oct 2026 (US), in force 13 to 16 Oct per TD World; read The National in full.
